Report No.: M20/R/EC/2026/01

Environment and Climate Change Committee

This Committee is the committee to which the Bill on the ... Amendment to Law No. 24/2022 (Waste Management Act), submitted on behalf of the Government by the Member for Ungoofaaru constituency, Ibrahim Shifaz, was sent for review, following the decision of the Committee of the Whole House, at its 2nd meeting of 2026 held on 15 July 2026, to send the bill to a sub-committee for review and to designate the Environment and Climate Change Committee as that sub-committee. The responsibility of this Committee is to make the necessary amendments to the above-mentioned bill, complete the bill, and then send it to the Committee of the Whole House, requesting that it be decided as that committee sees fit.

1. Introduction

This is the report on how this Committee reviewed and concluded the Bill on the ... Amendment to Law No. 24/2022 (Waste Management Act), submitted on behalf of the Government by the Member for Ungoofaaru constituency, Ibrahim Shifaz, following the decision of the Committee of the Whole House, at its 2nd meeting of 2026 held on 15 July 2026, to send the bill to a sub-committee for review and to designate the Environment and Climate Change Committee as that sub-committee, and to send the bill to this Committee.

The Bill on the ... Amendment to Law No. 24/2022 (Waste Management Act) was submitted to the People's Majlis on behalf of the Government by the Member for Ungoofaaru constituency, Ibrahim Shifaz. The first reading of this bill was held at the 11th sitting of the second session of 2026, held on 07 July 2026. The preliminary debate on the bill was also conducted at that same sitting. In addition, the debate on this bill continued at the 12th sitting of the second session of 2026, held on 08 July 2026, and at the 14th sitting of the second session of 2026, held on 14 July 2026. Further, at the 14th sitting of the second session of 2026, held on 14 July 2026, the Majlis voted to accept this bill with the unanimous agreement of the 57 (fifty-seven) members who took part in the vote, and the bill was sent to the Committee of the Whole House for review. Then, at that committee's 2nd meeting of 2026, held on 15 July 2026, that committee decided to send the bill to a sub-committee for review, to designate the Environment and Climate Change Committee as that sub-committee, and to send the bill to this Committee.

2. How the Committee reviewed the bill

Following the referral of this bill to the Committee, at this Committee's 7th meeting of 2026, held on 28 July 2026, the Committee members discussed how work on the bill would proceed, and the Committee decided that the deadline for the Committee to complete its work on the bill would be Monday, 10 August 2026. At this meeting the Committee also decided to open an opportunity for the public to submit their views on the bill until 03 August 2025 (Monday)

[signature]
[stamp]

and to send letters to the relevant offices listed below, seeking in writing any views or amendments they may wish to submit regarding the bill.

1. Ministry of Climate Change, Environment and Energy;
2. Ministry of Economic Development, Transport and Trade; and
3. Maldives Inland Revenue Authority.

In reviewing this bill, the Committee took into account the points raised by Committee members, the views submitted on the bill by the offices, and the views expressed by members of the People's Majlis at Majlis sittings regarding this bill. The Committee also read every article of the bill one by one, and decided to include in the bill the amendments that needed to be made to it.

A total of 5 Committee meetings were held to review this bill. At those meetings, Committee members spent approximately 2 hours and 34 minutes reviewing this bill.

3. Main amendments made to the bill by the Committee

After discussion among Committee members regarding this bill, the main amendments made to the bill by the Committee are set out below.

3.1 To remove from the bill the amendment proposed by Article 17 of the bill to amend Article 41 of Law No. 24/2022 (Waste Management Act).

| Article as it appears in the bill | 41. | (a) | Any party shall establish a waste management centre only in accordance with the standards set by the Ministry. |
| | | (b) | A site for landfilling as a means of waste management shall be established only in accordance with the standards set by the Ministry. |
| Amendment proposed by the Committee | To remove this amendment from the bill. |

[signature]
[stamp]

| Reason | The wording of the amendment proposed by Article 17 of the bill to Article 41 of Law No. 24/2022 (Waste Management Act) is the same as the wording of that article as it already stands in that Act. |

3.3 To amend paragraph (an) of Article 76 of Law No. 24/2022 (Waste Management Act), proposed for amendment by Article 28 of the bill, as follows.

| Article as it appears in the bill | 76. | (an) | "Plastic bag" means a bag made of plastic (including oxo-degradable plastic and self-degrading (degradable) plastic made from synthetic polymers) used for carrying goods, excluding bags in which goods are sealed. |
| Amendment proposed by the Committee | 76. | (an) | "Plastic bag" means a bag made of plastic (including oxo-degradable plastic and self-degrading (degradable) plastic made from synthetic polymers) used for carrying goods, excluding bags in which goods are sealed to the extent strictly necessary for selling those goods. |
| Reason | Because the proposed amendment refers to bags in which goods are sealed, putting goods into a bag and then tying a knot could also be regarded as sealing under that meaning; therefore, to state clearly in the law what a bag in which goods are sealed is. |

[signature]
[stamp]

3.2 To amend paragraph (bd) of Article 76 of Law No. 24/2022 (Waste Management Act), proposed to be added by Article 29 of the bill, as follows.

| Article as it appears in the bill | 76. | (bd) | "Organic peroxides" means liquid or solid substances whose chemical structure contains bivalent oxygen (-0-0-). |
| Amendment proposed by the Committee | 76. | (bd) | "Organic peroxides" means liquid or solid substances whose chemical structure contains bivalent oxygen (-0-0-) and which are flammable in themselves. |
| Reason | Because the way "organic peroxides" is defined in the proposed amendment does not make clear why waste arising from such substances is hazardous waste; therefore, to make this clear. |

4. Conclusion

After reviewing the Bill on the ... Amendment to Law No. 24/2022 (Waste Management Act) and discussing it among Committee members, the Committee, at its 11th meeting of 2026, held on 10 August 2026, passed the bill as reviewed and amended by the Committee, with the unanimous agreement of the members present at the Committee and taking part in the vote.

Accordingly, we submit this report requesting that the Committee of the Whole House decide as it sees fit on the Bill on the ... Amendment to Law No. 24/2022 (Waste Management Act), submitted on behalf of the Government by the Member for Ungoofaaru constituency, Ibrahim Shifaz, as passed by the Committee.

The "Bill on the ... Amendment to Law No. 24/2022 (Waste Management Act)", as amended and passed by the Committee, is set out as "Schedule-1" of this report.

[signature]
[stamp]

In addition, the details of attendance of Committee members at the meetings of this Committee held to review this bill are set out as "Schedule-2" of this report.

Bill on the ... Amendment to Law No. 24/2022 (Waste Management Act)

The following amendments are made to Law No. 24/2022 (Waste Management Act).

1. Amending paragraph (h) of Article 8 of the said Act as follows.

8. (h) Determining a waste management policy appropriate to islands and areas allocated for economic and/or industrial activities, suited to that island or that area;

2. Amending paragraph (p) of Article 8 of the said Act as follows.

8. (p) Designing and establishing waste management systems, and determining the standards to be maintained by those systems in managing waste;

3. Amending paragraph (q) of Article 8 of the said Act as follows.

8. (q) Determining the standards for establishing waste management centres and the standards for establishing centres that carry out the safe disposal of waste;

[signature]
[stamp]

4. Amending paragraph (r) of Article 8 of the said Act as follows.

8. (r) Formulating principles for determining the areas in which waste management centres and centres that carry out the safe disposal of waste are to be established;

5. Amending paragraph (s) of Article 8 of the said Act as follows.

8. (s) Determining the standards to be met by the facilities used to establish waste management systems, and the standards for testing and certifying those facilities;

6. Adding a paragraph after paragraph (s) of Article 8 of the said Act, as follows.

8. (t) Making all regulations required to implement this Act, and determining the standards that need to be determined.

7. Adding two paragraphs after paragraph (c) of Article 9 of the said Act, as follows.

9. (d) Planning and carrying out all matters required to implement the regulations made and the standards determined by the Ministry under this Act in relation to waste management;

(e) In cases where, as a result of waste management contrary to the standards determined by the Ministry under this Act, an adverse impact is caused to the environment and/or public health, fining the parties who act in that manner, in accordance with the regulation made under this Act by the Environmental Regulatory Authority.

[signature]
[stamp]

8. Amending paragraph (c) of Article 10 of the said Act as follows.

10. (c) Determining, in the regulation made under this Act, the standards and principles to be followed in providing waste management services, in accordance with the policies formulated and the standards and principles determined by the Ministry under this Act; implementing those principles and standards; and taking the necessary action against parties who contravene them;

9. Removing paragraph (d) of Article 10 of the said Act.

10. Amending paragraph (i) of Article 10 of the said Act as follows.

10. (i) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary stated in this Act or in any other law, ensuring that, in islands and areas allocated for economic and/or industrial activities, a waste management system appropriate to that island or that area is being operated sustainably; and

11. Amending the marginal heading of Article 12 of the said Act, and paragraph (a) of that article, as follows.

Management of waste generated in islands and areas allocated for economic or industrial activities
12. (a) The management of waste in islands and areas allocated for economic and/or industrial activities is the responsibility of the owner or the managing party of that island or that area.

[signature]
[stamp]

12. Amending Article 24 of the said Act as follows.

Plan for managing waste generated by economic activities
24. (a) An operational plan setting out how matters relating to the management of waste produced at places where tourism, agriculture, fisheries and other such economic activities are carried out will be conducted shall be formulated by the owner of that place or by the party managing that place, in accordance with the regulation made under this Act.

(b) Implementing the operational plan referred to in paragraph (a) of this article is the responsibility of the owner of that place or of the party managing that place.

(c) The operational plan for managing waste generated by economic activities prepared under paragraph (a) of this article shall be a plan formulated in accordance with the National Waste Management Master Plan and the island and city level or regional level waste management operational plan.

13. Adding an article after Article 24 of the said Act, as follows.

Industrial waste management plan
24-1 (a) An operational plan setting out how matters relating to the management of waste produced at places where industrial activities are carried out will be conducted shall be formulated by the owner of that place or by the party managing that place, in accordance with the regulation made under this Act.

(b) Implementing the operational plan referred to in paragraph (a) of this article is the responsibility of the owner of that place or of the party managing that place.

(c) The industrial waste management operational plan prepared under paragraph (a) of this article shall be a plan formulated in accordance with the National Waste Management Master Plan and the island and city level or regional

[signature]
[stamp]

level waste management operational plan.

14. Adding a paragraph after paragraph (b) of Article 25 of the said Act, as follows.

25. (c) The regulation made under paragraph (b) of this article shall, taking into account the types of waste specified under this Act, determine the categories of licences, and set out the principles and procedures for issuing a licence of each category, and the principles for determining additional conditions in licences so issued.

15. Adding a number after number (3) of paragraph (b) of Article 32 of the said Act, as follows.

32. (b) (4) Bundles of bags containing more than 50 (fifty) plastic bags.

16. Adding an article after Article 35 of the said Act, as follows.

Parties not registered with MIRA
35-1 (a) A regulation setting out the principles under which parties other than those registered for GST with MIRA shall spend the fee charged under this Act shall be formulated by the Ministry within 1 (one) year of the commencement of this Act, published in the Government Gazette, and made public on the Ministry's website.

(b) The Ministry shall ensure that, in accordance with this Act and the regulation made under this Act, parties other than those registered for GST with MIRA are charging the plastic bag fee in the course of business activities conducted in the Maldives.

[signature]
[stamp]

17. Amending paragraph (c) of Article 43 of the said Act as follows.

43. (c) Waste generated and produced in islands and areas where economic and/or industrial activities are carried out, which do not fall within the jurisdiction of an inhabited island of the Maldives, shall be taken to the waste management centre of an inhabited island of the Maldives only in the manner determined in the regulation made under this Act.

18. Removing paragraph (d) of Article 43 of the said Act.

19. Amending Article 44 of the said Act as follows.

Importing waste into the Maldives
44. It is an offence for any party to import waste of any kind into the Maldives.

20. Amending paragraph (c) of Article 47 of the said Act as follows.

47. (c) It is an offence for any party to sell, use or distribute in the Maldives hazardous waste or anything containing such waste, except in accordance with the regulations made by the Ministry under this Act and under a permit issued by the Environmental Regulatory Authority.

21. Amending paragraph (e) of Article 47 of the said Act as follows.

47. (e) In accordance with the regulations made by the Ministry under this Act, and by the Environmental Regulatory Authority

[signature] [stamp]

under a permit issued, hazardous waste shall not be recycled, have useful substances recovered from it, or otherwise be processed for any other purpose in the Maldives.

22. Amending paragraph (a) of Article 63 of the said Act as follows.

63. (a) If a party required to make a plan for managing waste generated by economic activities or an industrial waste management plan has not made such a plan, fining that party an amount not exceeding Rf 50,000/- (fifty thousand rufiyaa), by the Utility Regulatory Authority or by a party designated by the Utility Regulatory Authority.

23. Amending paragraph (b) of Article 64 of the said Act as follows.

64. (b) Notwithstanding anything stated in paragraph (a) of this article, if the party being fined is an island or city council, or if an offence specified in this Act has been committed in an area that does not fall within the jurisdiction of an island or city council, the money from the fine paid for such an offence shall be deposited into the "Maldives Green Fund" established under Law No. 3/2006 (Public Finance Act).

24. Amending paragraph (a) of Article 76 of the said Act as follows.

76. (a) "Waste" means anything that is discarded after its use has ended, or that is handed over to a particular party to be discarded. This includes solids, liquids and gases.

[signature] [stamp]

[Tracked-change margin, deleted: old item numbers 23, 24, 25]

25. Amending paragraph (v) of Article 76 of the said Act as follows.

76. (v) "Industrial waste" means waste produced or generated in the course of an industrial activity.

26. Amending paragraph (ah) of Article 76 of the said Act as follows.

76. (ah) "Environmental Regulatory Authority" means the "Environmental Regulatory Authority" operating under the government ministry assigned the responsibility of implementing policies relating to environmental protection.

27. Amending paragraph (an) of Article 76 of the said Act as follows.

76. (an) "Plastic bag" means a bag made of plastic (including oxo-degradable plastic and self-degrading (degradable) plastic made from synthetic polymers) used for carrying goods, excluding bags in which goods are sealed to the extent strictly necessary for selling those goods.

28. Adding the following paragraphs after paragraph (at) of Article 76 of the said Act.

76. (au) "Repair" means bringing a change to the material characteristics of items discarded as waste, for the purpose of reusing those items.

(av) "Explosive materials" or "explosives" means, at a certain temperature or pressure, poisons, poisonous gases, biological or chemical substances harmful to life, and

[signature] [stamp]

[Tracked-change margin, deleted: old item numbers 26, 27, 28, 29]

items or substances that explode in themselves.

(aw) "Flammable liquids" means substances of a kind that catch fire easily at the normal temperature of that environment by means of something used to light a fire or something that burns, or that catch fire easily in themselves at a certain temperature.

(ax) "Readily flammable solids" means solid substances, not included among explosive materials, that catch fire easily by means of something used to light a fire or something that burns, without being mixed with any chemical or mineral, or without any change being brought by the surrounding environment to the weight, volume or pressure of that thing.

(ba) "Substances liable to spontaneous combustion" means items or substances that catch fire easily when, during their carriage, their temperature rises in themselves at normal temperature or pressure, or when their temperature rises in the air.

(bb) "Substances which, in contact with water, catch fire or emit flammable gases" means substances which, when those items or substances come into contact with water, catch fire in themselves or emit a gas that can catch fire.

(bc) "Items or substances that, by producing oxygen, facilitate the combustion of another item or substance" means items or substances which, even if they do not catch fire in themselves, by producing oxygen, enable another item or substance

[signature] [stamp]

to catch fire.

(bd) "Organic peroxides" means liquid or solid substances whose chemical structure contains bivalent oxygen (-0-0-) and which are flammable in themselves.

(be) "Toxic substances" means substances which, as a result of entering the human body or coming into contact with the skin, may cause loss of life, or cause temporary disability or permanent harm to humans or living organisms.

(bf) "Infectious substances" means substances that carry, or are capable of carrying, pathogens that transmit disease to humans or living organisms, or that contain such a dangerous thing.

(bg) "Corrosives" means substances which, when they come into contact with a part of the body or with anything, cause serious damage to the part of the body or the thing they came into contact with, as a result of the chemical reaction that occurs.

(bh) "Ecotoxic substances" means substances or items which, as a result of being released into the environment, cause harm in the short or long term to the living organisms in that place through the absorption and accumulation of that substance in their bodies.

(bi) "Economic activities" means activities carried out in tourism, agriculture, fisheries and other economic sectors.

[signature] [stamp]

29. Changing the places in the said Act where "Agency" is stated to "Environmental Regulatory Authority", and changing the places where "Authority" is stated to "Utility Regulatory Authority".

30. The amendments required to be made to the regulations formulated under the said Act as a result of the amendments brought to that Act by this Act, and the regulations newly required to be formulated under that Act, shall be formulated within 30 (thirty) days from the date of commencement of this Act and published in the Government Gazette.

31. This Act shall come into force on the day it is passed, ratified and published in the Government Gazette.
